document.editionNote: The plan prints no date of its own and the PDF carries no metadata at all (pdfinfo shows no Title, Creator, Producer, CreationDate or ModDate). The latest event its text cites is the NGT order of 17.09.2019 in O.A. 829/2019 (page 28). The scanned signature page (29) carries the District Collector's signature with a pink-ink mark beside it reading like '6/5', and a separate blue-ink initial hand-dated 25/11/19; the listing page on tiruvallur.nic.in shows Publish Date 05/12/2019 and the file sits under a December 2019 upload path (uploads/2019/12/2019120533.pdf). The CDN's HTTP Last-Modified (29 Feb 2020) is the hosting migration, not the document. The hand-dated initial is taken as the document date and the edition is labelled 2019; site search and the Documents listing on 2026-09-06 show no other edition.
document.template: CPCB model District Environmental Plan under NGT O.A. No. 710-713/2017 (order dated 15.07.2019): a cover, an index, an Introduction (NGT order, the 19-member District Committee, the list of subjects) followed by eleven subject sections: solid waste, bio-medical waste, plastic waste, C&D waste, polluted river stretches, industrial pollution control, utilisation of treated sewage, conservation of water bodies, e-waste, illegal sand mining, and coastal and marine pollution, each a short preamble followed by a responsibility / plan-of-action / stakeholders table. It prints no demand, supply or deficit water balance.
quirks: The cover cites Hon'ble NGT order in O.A.No.710-713/2017 dated 15.07.2019, and the preamble the D.O. letter of 26.07.2019 that followed it, rather than O.A. 360/2018.

The cover prints 'TIRUVALLUR DISTRICT' above 'District Environmental Plan' with the Tamil Nadu emblem and a photograph of the collectorate building but no office name in its text; the comma in the title here is added, and the publisher is taken from the District Committee list on page 4 and the 'District Collector Tiruvallur' signature block on page 29.
Every page carries a footer number equal to its PDF page number (the cover is page 1), and the index page numbers match, so printedPage equals pdfPage throughout.
The PDF has no document metadata of any kind: pdfinfo prints no Title, Author, Creator, Producer, CreationDate or ModDate.

Page 29 is a scanned image with no text layer (pdftotext returns nothing for it); it carries the last two rows of the coastal-pollution table (industrial units along the coast to treat sewage and trade effluent; no dumping of solid waste into the coastal and marine area) and the signature block, so its action points cannot be quoted from the text.

The plan is hosted as a post under 'Uncategorized' at /district-environmental-plan/ (breadcrumb Home > Uncategorized > District Environmental Plan) with 'Publish Date : 05/12/2019'; the site's Documents listing does not carry it.

Section 12, Prevention of Coastal and Marine Pollution, is the one section beyond the eleven CPCB subjects; it cites the NGT order dated 17.09.2019 in O.A. No. 829/2019, spells the district 'Thiruvallur', prints 'Hob'ble NGT' and 'Treated effluent shall copy with the Standards', and names Pulicat lake, thermal power plants, the port and petroleum terminals as the monitored CRZ installations.
No district sewage-generation figure, district STP or STP capacity is printed; the treated-sewage section gives only the Tamil Nadu totals (5600 MLD generated, 54 STPs of 1400 MLD).

The industrial-pollution action table on page 16 lists 'No of ETPs required', 'No of ETPs provided', 'No of STPs required for the local bodies' and 'No of STPs provided in the local bodies' as items but prints no numbers against them.

The water-bodies table on page 20 is statewide only (90,048 available, 5607 rejuvenated, 1806 under rejuvenation); the district's own count is not printed. The RDD row prints a dash in the under-rejuvenation column and the HR&CE row alone uses a thousands comma (2,359).
The water-bodies preamble misquotes the NGT threshold as 'water bodies having area less than 0.5 acre or more as recorded in the revenue record'.
The Kosasthalaiyar is spelled 'Kosathalaiyar' on page 14 and 'Kosasthalaiyar' on pages 21 and 26; 'Red hills' (the Puzhal reservoir) appears without 'reservoir' in the main-water-bodies list.

The district is described as 1 Corporation, 4 Municipalities, 10 Town Panchayats and 14 Panchayat Unions (page 5), with 526 village panchayats (page 11); the solid-waste authorisation row fills '11' for both eligible ULBs and ULBs holding authorisation but leaves its 'as on' dates blank, and the plastic-waste registration row leaves both counts and dates blank.
The action tables carry no priority column, so every action point's priority is null.
Bulleted lines on page 14 carry a private-use bullet glyph (U+F0D8) in the text extraction; quotes start after it.
Curly apostrophes come through the text layer as a low double quote ('Hon‟ble', 'doesn‟t'); quotes here are taken from that text as is.

actionPoints.text: To carry out Air Quality Monitoring, Water Quality Monitoring (ground water) & Compost quality in and around processing facilities & dumpsites as per Schedule I & II of SWM Rules, 2016 at all Corporations and sensitive / ecological Municipalities; periodicity of water quality monitoring: summer, monsoon, post-monsoon.

Special Task Force shall periodically review once in two weeks on the status of creating awareness and also on the prevention of dumping of solid waste and discharge of sewage in water bodies, action against open burning of solid wastes, etc.

PWD, Revenue and Local body officers are advised to ensure that all the encroachments are removed in the important rivers such as Cooum, Kosathalaiyar, Araniyar; TNPC Board directed to monitor any industrial discharge into the said rivers; local bodies directed to ensure that no sewage is discharged into the river.

No of ETPs required in and provided in Industries (Red/Orange/17 category); No of STPs required for and provided in the local bodies; functional status of ETPs/STPs; monitoring of treated effluent qualities of ETPs/STPs.
All the municipalities and Town Panchayat shall cover their entire jurisdiction area under UGDS scheme. Sewage received in STP shall be treated to the Discharge standards.
Periodic monitoring of treated sewage with preferably online monitoring (parameters for analysis pH, BOD, TSS, TDS, COD, Total N, Fecal Coliform).

Industries located near Common STP shall make MoU with the operator of STP so as to utilize treated sewage to meet their industrial requirement after proper tertiary treatment; treated sewage from the Common STPs shall be utilized for industrial use, agriculture, ground water recharge and other non-domestic use.

Collection of catchment and lead channel pollution data, sewage disposal contamination data, industrial effluent disposal data, solid waste, plastic waste, e-waste, hazardous waste and C & D waste disposal data for all the Water Bodies.

Declaring the Designated Best use of water bodies and ascertain the quality of water as per the standard; survey to identify the source of pollution and prepare long term preventive measures on sewage, industrial effluent and solid waste management; deweeding, desilting, protection of drainage basin, channels, stabilization of earthen bunds and preparing cost estimation.
Removal of encroachments and blockades, deciding on flood control measures and preparing cost estimation.

Identification of river stretches where there are chances for illegal sand mining; frequent surprise checks in those river stretches by the Taluk Level Task Force and submit reports to District Level Task Force fortnightly; District Level Task Force shall meet once in a month.

No untreated sewage / trade effluent shall be let out into coastal and marine water bodies: local / urban local bodies along the sea coast shall set up sewage treatment plants (STPs) of adequate capacity including provision for sewerage system to cover the entire local / urban areas; treated effluent shall comply with the standards.
